description.value: The study examined cerebral glucose metabolism and 5-HT2A receptor distribution in patients with the apathetic and disinhibited behavioral syndromes of the frontal variant of frontotemporal lobar degeneration.

spans.text: This study had two primary goals: (1) to test the hypothesis that different behavioral aspects in fv-FTLD are caused by degeneration of selective frontal areas, which is reflected in different patterns of brain glucose hypometabolism; and (2) to measure cerebral 5-HT2A receptor densities in the same patients in the early phase of the disease, using PET and [11C]MDL100,907, because no in vivo data about this receptor subtype are available in the fv-FTLD.

design.value: A cross-sectional PET study compared resting-state cerebral glucose uptake in 18 patients with fv-FTLD and 24 healthy control subjects, including comparisons of apathetic and disinhibited patient subgroups; [11C]MDL100,907 PET receptor-binding data were compared between eight fv-FTLD patients and six healthy volunteers.

spans.text: We studied cerebral glucose uptake using (18)F-fluorodeoxyglucose and positron emission tomography in 18 patients fulfilling clinical criteria for fv-FTLD and showing, respectively, an apathetic or disinhibited behavioral syndrome.
In eight of these patients, we also evaluated the 5-hydroxytryptamine-2A receptor cerebral receptor distribution with [(11)C]MDL and positron emission tomography.

The following statistical comparisons were performed on 18FDG images: (1) the main effect of the whole fv-FTLD group compared with the healthy control subjects; (2) direct comparisons between the two groups and the healthy control subjects (apathetic fv-FTLD patients vs control group; disinhibited fv-FTLD patients vs control group); (3) direct comparisons between apathetic and disinhibited groups (apathetic vs disinhibited patients; disinhibited vs apathetic patients); and (4) correlation analyses between disease duration and metabolic values in the whole group and in the subgroups separately.
